facts.arm: The arm connects the shoulder to the hand and lets you reach and lift.
facts.ear: The ear is the organ used for hearing and keeping your balance.
facts.eye: The eye is the organ that lets you see light, color, and shape.
facts.hip: The hip is the joint connecting the leg to the pelvis.
facts.jaw: The jaw is the bone structure that holds the teeth and lets you chew.
facts.leg: The leg supports the body's weight and allows walking and running.
facts.lip: The lip is the soft edge around the mouth used for speaking and eating.
facts.rib: A rib is one of the curved bones that protect the chest and lungs.
facts.toe: A toe is one of the small digits at the end of the foot.
facts.gum: The gum is the pink tissue that surrounds and supports the teeth.
facts.back: The back is the rear part of the body, from the neck to the hips.
facts.chin: The chin is the front part of the jaw below the mouth.
facts.foot: The foot is at the end of the leg and supports the body while standing.
facts.hand: The hand is at the end of the arm and is used for grasping and touching.
facts.head: The head contains the brain and most of the sense organs.
facts.heel: The heel is the back part of the foot, below the ankle.
facts.knee: The knee is the joint that bends between the thigh and the lower leg.
facts.neck: The neck connects the head to the shoulders and supports the head.
facts.shin: The shin is the front edge of the lower leg, just below the knee.
facts.palm: The palm is the inner, flat surface of the hand.
facts.bone: A bone is a hard structure that forms part of the skeleton.
facts.calf: The calf is the muscle at the back of the lower leg.
facts.lobe: The lobe is the soft, rounded lower part of the outer ear.
facts.nail: A nail is the hard covering that protects the tip of a finger or toe.
facts.nose: The nose is used for breathing and smelling.
facts.skin: Skin is the body's largest organ and covers and protects the body.
facts.vein: A vein is a blood vessel that carries blood back toward the heart.
facts.womb: The womb is the organ in a woman's body where a baby grows before birth.
facts.iris: The iris is the colored ring around the pupil that controls light entering the eye.
facts.lung: A lung is one of two organs in the chest used for breathing.
facts.ankle: The ankle is the joint connecting the foot to the lower leg.
facts.brain: The brain is the organ in the head that controls thought and the body.
facts.chest: The chest is the front part of the upper body, containing the heart and lungs.
facts.elbow: The elbow is the joint in the middle of the arm that lets it bend.
facts.heart: The heart is the muscle that pumps blood around the body.
facts.liver: The liver is a large organ that helps digest food and clean the blood.
facts.mouth: The mouth is the opening used for eating, drinking, and speaking.
facts.skull: The skull is the bony structure that protects the brain.
facts.spine: The spine is the column of bones that runs down the back and supports the body.
facts.thumb: The thumb is the short, thick digit on the hand, opposite the fingers.
facts.cheek: The cheek is the soft side of the face below the eye.
facts.colon: The colon is part of the large intestine that absorbs water from digested food.
facts.gland: A gland is an organ that produces and releases substances such as hormones.
facts.groin: The groin is the area where the abdomen meets the thigh.
facts.joint: A joint is where two bones meet and allow the body to bend or move.
facts.nerve: A nerve carries signals between the brain and the rest of the body.
facts.pupil: The pupil is the small black opening in the eye that lets light in.
facts.thigh: The thigh is the part of the leg between the hip and the knee.
facts.torso: The torso is the trunk of the body, not counting the head, arms, and legs.
facts.wrist: The wrist is the joint connecting the hand to the forearm.
facts.finger: A finger is one of the five digits on the hand.
facts.kidney: A kidney is one of two organs that filter waste from the blood into urine.
facts.muscle: A muscle is tissue that contracts to move the bones and organs of the body.
facts.pelvis: The pelvis is the bony structure at the base of the spine that supports the hips.
facts.temple: The temple is the flat area on the side of the head, near the forehead.
facts.throat: The throat is the passage in the neck used for breathing and swallowing.
facts.tonsil: A tonsil is a small gland at the back of the throat that helps fight infection.
facts.tongue: The tongue is the muscle in the mouth used for tasting, chewing, and speaking.
facts.armpit: The armpit is the hollow area underneath where the arm meets the shoulder.
facts.spleen: The spleen is an organ that filters blood and supports the immune system.
facts.retina: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye.
facts.cornea: The cornea is the clear outer layer that covers the front of the eye.
facts.larynx: The larynx, or voice box, is in the throat and produces the voice.
facts.tendon: A tendon is tough tissue that connects muscle to bone.
facts.biceps: The biceps is the muscle at the front of the upper arm.
facts.rectum: The rectum is the final section of the large intestine, near the anus.
facts.thorax: The thorax is another name for the chest, the area between the neck and abdomen.
facts.marrow: Marrow is the soft tissue inside bones that produces blood cells.
facts.fibula: The fibula is the thinner of the two bones in the lower leg.
facts.radius: The radius is one of the two bones in the forearm, on the thumb side.
facts.abdomen: The abdomen is the part of the body between the chest and the pelvis.
facts.forearm: The forearm is the part of the arm between the elbow and the wrist.
facts.kneecap: The kneecap is the small bone that covers and protects the front of the knee.
facts.eardrum: The eardrum is the thin tissue that vibrates inside the ear to let us hear.
facts.nostril: A nostril is one of the two openings in the nose used for breathing.
facts.knuckle: A knuckle is a joint in the finger where it bends.
facts.sternum: The sternum, or breastbone, is the flat bone in the middle of the chest.
facts.trachea: The trachea, or windpipe, carries air from the throat to the lungs.
facts.stomach: The stomach is the organ that digests food after it is swallowed.
facts.bladder: The bladder is the organ that stores urine before it leaves the body.
facts.thyroid: The thyroid is a gland in the neck that helps control the body's metabolism.
facts.cranium: The cranium is the part of the skull that encloses and protects the brain.
facts.jawbone: The jawbone holds the teeth in place and lets the mouth open and close.
facts.patella: The patella is the medical name for the kneecap.
facts.scapula: The scapula, or shoulder blade, is the flat bone at the back of the shoulder.
facts.humerus: The humerus is the long bone in the upper arm, between the shoulder and elbow.
facts.triceps: The triceps is the muscle at the back of the upper arm.
facts.cochlea: The cochlea is the spiral-shaped part of the inner ear that helps us hear.
facts.toenail: A toenail is the hard covering that protects the tip of a toe.
facts.midriff: The midriff is the middle part of the body around the waist and lower ribs.
